items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: I had my trio working with Joe, which was Bob Cranshaw and Mickey Roker and myself.

ctx.x: What was it like working with Joe?

With Joe it was great. I knew Joe from Chicago anyway, Joe lived, I think he grew up in Chicago, he was born in Georgia. And it was a good experience working with Joe. I had my trio working with Joe, which was Bob Cranshaw and Mickey Roker and myself. And we had a good time. We had the same manager, John Levy, and he thought it was a good idea to put the two together, to solve two things. We usually played a short set before Joe came on and then played for Joe. And that was a good experience. I really liked…
Nat told us some great stories about some of his compositions.

items.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: and then that’s when I joined Joe Williams’ band with the Junior Mance Trio.

ctx.x: Well I played rhythm & blues in Philly with a band, a guy named King James. I did that for a year in a group with Jimmy Devine called the High Five. We had a band together for about a year, and then I decided that playing that way is so limited you know. So I devoted my life to playing jazz because it’s more free, it’s open you know, and you can express more rhythm. So then I started playing with people like Sam Reed, all these Philadelphia musicians, and Jimmy Heath and Jimmy Oliver. Jimmy Heath is the guy that…
play with Gigi Gryce. So I played with Gigi Gryce for a couple of years, played with Ray Bryant for a couple of years, and then that’s when I joined Joe Williams’ band with the Junior Mance Trio.
Tell us about Joe. How do you feel his voice typifies jazz vocals?
